But as soon as I got into beginner pilates/barre, I noticed instructors have a habit of “wooting” whenever a set gets hard (which is often in a 30 min workout). It’s loud into the mic, and repetitive. It was the same with the PVolve app, to the point where I had to mute the workouts. Love this app, love the great, effective workouts, but the same loud sounds on repeat are distracting and irritating when you’re trying to concentrate and push through.

reviews.title: Senada is amazing, but the app is unfortunately lazy
reviews.text: Senada is great. I’ll start there. But, the app needs to improve, to the point I cancelled my membership because of it. Weight tracking auto-populates (not to what I tracked for that exercise last session), but rather the weight from the unrelated exercise preceding it in the current sequence; the exercise descriptions are minimal, leaving much to be desired regarding important form cues, so you’re forced to study the video, which is problematic because the app will occasionally freeze and quit in the middle of a workout, particularly on videos. Last, the menstrual cycle remains toggled on despite saving it in the off position. More cons than pros, unfortunately. In the age of AI I’d expect significantly better than this.

reviews.title: Deeply misleading and incredibly disappointing.
reviews.text:
I signed up for WeRise after going through one of its click-funnel surveys, largely because I follow the founder on Instagram and genuinely respect her work. The marketing was extremely clear: this was presented as a program for people with very limited time — even framed around having as little as 30 minutes a week to work out while still making meaningful progress.

That promise was the entire reason I subscribed. I was explicit in the survey about what I needed: an efficient program that respected my time. Instead, once I paid for the app — and was locked into a one-year subscription — I found that the workouts being served to me were nowhere near what had been advertised. The shortest workouts were around 45 minutes, with many running well over an hour, and that was before adding the so-called “optional” warm-up or cool-down.

To make matters worse, there was also a money-back guarantee tied to a trial period, yet my refund request was denied even though I made it within the 30-day window. So not only did the product fail to deliver what was promised, but the company also failed to honor the safety net that made the purchase feel lower-risk in the first place.

The app itself is also clunky and frustrating to use. The user experience is poor, the onboarding feels manipulative, and the actual product does not match the sales pitch.

This is not just disappointing — it feels deceptive. Beware of the marketing. What is promised and what is delivered are not the same.

reviews.title: Great but needs work
reviews.text: This is a great app especially for beginners who are new in the gym and not sure what to do or use for what muscle area your working on. There are how ever a few things that may need fixing, starting with the self care videos, the few I was able to watch were great and very motivating and nice to listen to, but I was only able to watch 3 videos before it stopped playing for me. It literally just shows a black screen no sound and that’s it. I even updated the app and still nothing. An other thing that I hope happens is that the work outs may need to be organized better, I don’t have an at home gym with special machines, I use a gym open to the public; the last time I completed a day it used one specific machine and then would move on to a different exercise before having me go back to that same machine again about maybe 3 or 4 times I ended up having to go back to  the machine. It had me do cable seated rows, then crunches, then rope pull downs, then leg raises, then cable face pulls, then table top rows, I get the purpose because sometimes while “resting” after a specific exercise you do a different exercise so your body doesn’t fully relax too much but I can’t just lay in the middle of a aisle at the gym to complete and exercise it’s hazardous and selfish to take up space like that. Last but not least, I’m not sure of maybe I’m missing something or not but I wish there was a way to switch out exercises mid session that would be great for when I do last minute gym sessions with someone else and when they can’t do a certain machine or exercise I always want to try and accommodate while not sacrificing me working on the muscle. I’ve never tried the recipe part of the app but they seem pretty solid and great when trying to look for some healthy ideas.
